provenance: Original synthetic teaching inputs, created 2026-10-08. No observed company, security, market quote, tax jurisdiction or lender commitment is represented.
timing: All operating receipts, payments, tax, investment and financing changes occur in a synchronized year-end batch. Debt and cash interest use opening balances. End-year capex starts service next year; the supplied depreciation schedule is the asset-register assumption. No within-year funding claim is made.

pricing.assumption: Illustrative project-risk inputs imply an operating required return of 10%. Each scenario is a conditional expected operating forecast, not a complete set of priced states. No scenario probabilities are supplied. All excluded financial cash is worth par and earns its own 4% required return; retaining it has no additional agency or transaction cost. Debt market quotes are supplied separately and are not inferred from promised coupons or these two sensitivities.

terminal.assumption: At the start of year 4 the current backlog cycle normalizes. All opening operating capital earns the return implied by turnover, margin, depreciation and tax. Capital and NOPAT then grow at 2%; end-year net reinvestment equals growth times opening capital. No liquidation or wholesale working-capital release occurs.

finance.contract: These are fictional enforceable contracts with no fees, transaction costs or tax shields. The term debt is retained at acquisition; consent is supplied and no change-of-control acceleration exists. At ends 1/2, after scheduled term amortization, total term plus revolving debt cannot exceed 1.75 times that year's EBITDA; the revolver outstanding cannot exceed 120. Minimum cash 30 applies at all modeled dates. Surplus cash repays the revolver first; if it reaches zero, remaining cash is retained. All remaining term and revolving principal must be paid at end 3. A signed replacement commitment then issues an undated fixed-coupon note at par for only the amount needed to restore cash 30. Its face cannot exceed 80 or 1.75 times normalized year 4 EBITDA, and prior compliance is required. It pays 6% annually from end 4, with no scheduled principal repayment; no uncommitted renewal is assumed. No new equity after date 0 is authorized. Initial and later payouts must satisfy every applicable constraint. Operating EBIT tax is 25%, interest is nondeductible, and the 4% cash return is already after tax. No leases, preferred claims, pensions, noncontrolling interests or other target claims exist.

peers.measurement: Complete supplied candidate universe at date 0. All money kCU. Forward year 1 EBITDA uses the same forecast vintage and full consolidation perimeter; debt and NCI are market claim values. All financial cash and nonoperating holdings are excluded from operating EV. No leases. Adjustments are supplied one-off evidence assumptions, not universal accounting permissions. Normalized margin for Nacre forward year 1 is 18%, applied to that scenario's year 1 revenue; the base backlog contribution 12 is temporary.

candidates.evidence: Software subscription platform with customer-acquisition economics and capital intensity unlike the physical manufacturers.

candidates.name: Vesper Devices
candidates.evidence: Financially distressed manufacturer with negative normalized EBITDA. Its distress remains relevant to the risk discussion.
candidates.reason: Negative denominator is unsuitable for this positive-profit multiple comparison; do not hide the candidate.

limits: No empirical estimate, legal opinion, general reporting engine, full default-pricing model or probabilistic expected-NPV claim.
The pricing model is an operating-asset valuation approximation with supplied risk assumptions; debt quotes and contractual funding feasibility are separate inputs.
Annual synchronized payments do not establish intrayear liquidity. Required cash is an excluded financial asset earning its own fair return, not operating NWC or an extra terminal cash-flow release.
The replacement note is an explicit indefinite obligation whose coupon remains in future treasury cash, not free cash or an omitted maturity.
